input: prices is a list of n integers in [0, 4503599627370495], with 0 <= n <= 4294967295. Values are successive daily prices. Integers are plain int values, excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists rather than subclasses; strings are ordinary str values. Standard built-ins are unmodified and no concurrent mutation occurs. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds do not guarantee allocation capacity or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The maximum integer profit from at most two completed buy/sell transactions, at most one share held at a time, with no fee or cooldown. Transactions are temporally ordered and cannot overlap. A sell and a new buy at the same daily price are permitted and add no artificial gain. Empty or singleton input returns 0; only profit is returned.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. Four scalar running states represent the first acquisition, first completed profit, effective second acquisition and second completed profit. No transaction history or output container is allocated.
numeric: Let B = 4503599627370495. first_cost and first_profit stay in [0, B]; second_cost stays in [-B, B]. Every price-first_cost and price-first_profit lies in [-B, B], and price-second_cost lies in [-B, 2*B]. All intermediates and second_profit are within the safe range because 2*B = 9007199254740990. State updates on the same day permit only zero-duration, zero-profit transitions and do not add a third transaction.
complexity: O(n + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Process prices once, in dependency order from the first buy through the second sell. This is a two-transaction dynamic program, not the unlimited-transactions sum-of-rises algorithm.
